1	# Feature Specification: Rooms List Shows the Right Rooms on Every Page
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: none — no branch hook is installed; the work stays on `main` (feature directory `specs/003-fix-rooms-pagination`)
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-11-10
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "Bug report: the rooms page shows the wrong rooms on page 2." On the `/rooms` page with 5 rooms per page, page 2 shows `Room 11` and `Room 12`; `GET /api/rooms?page=2&limit=5` returns the same. Expected: with 12 rooms ordered by name and 5 per page, page 2 shows `Room 06` to `Room 10` and page 3 shows `Room 11` and `Room 12`; paging must be right for every page and every allowed page size. Known: page 1 looks right at every page size, and page 2 is right at the default 10 per page. Asked: (1) analyse the bug and write up the cause before changing any code — where it is, why it happens, why the existing tests did not catch it; (2) fix it; (3) add a regression test that fails without the fix. Done when `GET /api/rooms?page=2&limit=5` returns `Room 06` to `Room 10` and `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run test` pass.
10	
11	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
12	
13	### User Story 1 - Browse every room at any page size (Priority: P1)
14	
15	Someone looking for a meeting room opens the rooms list, picks how many rooms they want per page and walks through the pages. Each page shows the next rooms in name order, so that after the last page they have seen every room exactly once. Today, at any page size other than 10, the pages after the first show the wrong rooms: some rooms are never shown and the last rooms appear too early.
16	
17	**Why this priority**: This is the reported defect. Rooms that never appear cannot be found or booked from the list, and the list contradicts its own page counter.
18	
19	**Independent Test**: With the 12 seeded rooms, request the rooms list at 5 per page and walk pages 1 to 3, on the `/rooms` page and through `GET /api/rooms`; compare the rooms on each page with the expected slice of the name-ordered list.
20	
21	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
22	
23	1. **Given** 12 rooms named `Room 01` to `Room 12`, **When** page 2 is requested with 5 rooms per page, **Then** the result is `Room 06`, `Room 07`, `Room 08`, `Room 09`, `Room 10`, in that order.
24	2. **Given** the same 12 rooms, **When** page 3 is requested with 5 rooms per page, **Then** the result is `Room 11` and `Room 12`.
25	3. **Given** the same 12 rooms, **When** page 1 is requested with 5 rooms per page, **Then** the result is `Room 01` to `Room 05` (unchanged).
26	4. **Given** the same 12 rooms, **When** page 2 is requested with the default 10 rooms per page, **Then** the result is `Room 11` and `Room 12` (unchanged).
27	5. **Given** the same 12 rooms and any allowed page size, **When** every page from 1 to the last is read in turn, **Then** each room appears exactly once and the rooms are in name order across the pages.
28	6. **Given** the `/rooms` page, **When** the user chooses 5 rooms per page and goes to page 2, **Then** the table shows `Room 06` to `Room 10`.
29	
30	---
31	
32	### User Story 2 - The cause is written down before the fix (Priority: P2)
33	
34	The owner of the system wants to know why the defect happened and why it shipped unnoticed, before any code is changed. A written analysis names where the defect is, why it produces the observed rooms, and why the existing tests passed in spite of it.
35	
36	**Why this priority**: The fix is small, but the test gap that let it through is the lasting risk; the analysis is what makes the regression test target the right thing.
37	
38	**Independent Test**: Read the analysis and check that it explains all four reported observations (page 1 right at every size, page 2 right at 10 per page, page 2 wrong at 5 per page, page 2 at 5 per page showing exactly `Room 11` and `Room 12`), and that the change history shows it was written before the code change.
39	
40	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
41	
42	1. **Given** the bug report, **When** the analysis is finished, **Then** it states where the defect is, why it happens, and why the existing tests did not catch it, and no code has been changed yet.
43	2. **Given** the analysis, **When** its explanation is checked against the four reported observations, **Then** it accounts for each of them.
44	
45	---
46	
47	### User Story 3 - The defect cannot come back unnoticed (Priority: P3)
48	
49	A developer who later changes the rooms list is told by the automated tests if paging breaks again for a page size other than the default.
50	
51	**Why this priority**: Without it the same defect can return silently, as the existing tests only exercise the default page size beyond page 1.
52	
53	**Independent Test**: Run the new regression test against the code as it is today and see it fail; run it again after the fix and see it pass.
54	
55	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
56	
57	1. **Given** the code before the fix, **When** the regression test runs, **Then** it fails.
58	2. **Given** the code after the fix, **When** the full test suite runs, **Then** the regression test and all existing tests pass.
59	
60	---
61	
62	### Edge Cases
63	
64	- A page past the last one (for example page 4 at 5 per page): the result has no rooms and still reports the total of 12, as today.
65	- The last page is partly filled (page 3 at 5 per page holds 2 rooms).
66	- The page size equals or exceeds the number of rooms (12 or more per page): page 1 holds all rooms and page 2 is empty.
67	- The smallest allowed page size (1 per page): page N holds exactly the Nth room in name order.
68	- No page or page size is given: page 1 with 10 rooms per page, as today.
69	- A page or page size outside the allowed range is still rejected as invalid input, as today.
70	
71	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
72	
73	### Functional Requirements
74	
75	- **FR-001**: For page number P and page size L, the rooms list MUST return the rooms at positions (P − 1) × L + 1 through P × L of all rooms ordered by name ascending, or as many of them as exist.
76	- **FR-002**: FR-001 MUST hold for every allowed page number (1 and above) and every allowed page size (1 to 100), not only the default page size.
77	- **FR-003**: Reading every page in turn at a fixed page size MUST show each room exactly once, with no room skipped or repeated.
78	- **FR-004**: The `/rooms` page MUST show the rooms defined by FR-001 for the page and rows-per-page the user selected.
79	- **FR-005**: The result MUST keep reporting the total number of rooms, the requested page and the requested page size, as today.
80	- **FR-006**: Everything else about the rooms list MUST stay as it is: ordering by name, the default of page 1 with 10 per page, rejection of out-of-range input, and the shape of the response.
81	- **FR-007**: A written root-cause analysis MUST exist before any code is changed, covering where the defect is, why it happens, and why the existing tests did not catch it.
82	- **FR-008**: A regression test MUST be added that fails against the code before the fix and passes after it, and that exercises a page beyond the first at a page size other than the default.
83	- **FR-009**: The fix MUST be limited to the defect: no new routes, fields, error codes or dependencies, and no change to bookings.
84	
85	### Key Entities
86	
87	- **Room**: a bookable meeting room; the list is ordered by its name. Twelve rooms, `Room 01` to `Room 12`, are seeded.
88	- **Page of rooms**: one slice of the name-ordered room list, together with the total number of rooms, the page number and the page size it was requested with.
89	
90	## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
91	
92	### Measurable Outcomes
93	
94	- **SC-001**: Requesting page 2 at 5 rooms per page returns exactly `Room 06` to `Room 10`, through the API and on the `/rooms` page.
95	- **SC-002**: For the 12 seeded rooms and each of the page sizes 1, 5, 10, 12 and 100, walking all pages yields all 12 rooms exactly once in name order: 0 rooms missing, 0 duplicated.
96	- **SC-003**: The root-cause analysis explains 4 out of 4 reported observations and predates the code change in the change history.
97	- **SC-004**: The regression test fails before the fix and passes after it.
98	- **SC-005**: The project's three quality gates (build, lint, test) all pass with the fix in place.
99	
100	## Assumptions
101	
102	- "Allowed page size" means the range the system already accepts: 1 to 100, default 10. Page numbers start at 1. These limits are not changed.
103	- A page past the last one returns an empty list with the correct total rather than an error; this is today's behaviour and is kept.
104	- Room names are unique and sort as text, so `Room 01` to `Room 12` have one well-defined order.
105	- The bookings list is out of scope: the report concerns rooms only. If the analysis finds the same defect elsewhere, it is recorded in the analysis and not fixed in this change.
106	- The `/rooms` page shows whatever the API returns for the selected page and page size; if the analysis confirms this, the frontend needs no change, only the service behind the API.
107	- The root-cause analysis is written during planning as the feature's research document (`specs/003-fix-rooms-pagination/research.md`), before the implementation step; this specification does not state the cause.
108	- Verification uses the 12 seeded rooms; no data migration or new seed data is needed.

28	
29	- `libs/contract` (`@roombook/contract`) is the source of truth for routes, message patterns,

31	- Code MUST use what `@roombook/contract` exports. A route, pattern, field or error code
32	  MUST NOT be invented outside it.
33	- Errors MUST cross service boundaries as `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }`, with
34	  `errorCode` taken from `ErrorCodeEnum`.
35	
36	Rationale: the gateway, the NATS services, the worker and the frontend stay compatible only
37	when they all read the same definitions.
38

40	
41	- Controllers MUST be thin: at most five statements, all delegating to a service. Controllers
42	  MUST NOT contain logic.
43	- Every POST, PUT and PATCH handler MUST take a DTO class with class-validator decorators as
44	  its body.
45	- Services hold business rules and MUST delegate data access to repositories.
46	- Database transactions MUST live in repositories only, never in services.
47	- The gateway MUST NOT hold database access or business rules; it validates input and forwards
48	  over NATS.
49	- Every controller, service and provider MUST be registered in exactly one module.
50	- Source files MUST NOT contain literal ports, hosts, URLs or secrets; configuration comes from
51	  environment variables read through the config module.
52	- Every deployable service MUST have a health endpoint: a health message pattern on each NATS
53	  service, exposed by the gateway as `GET /api/health/<service>`.
54	
55	Rationale: each layer has one responsibility, so a rule has one place to live and one place
56	to be tested.
57

59	
60	- `interface` MUST NOT be used; use `class` for DTOs and `type` for everything else.
61	- `any` MUST NOT be used.
62	- An inline object type MUST NOT be used as a function parameter; define a named DTO class.
63	- Every repository method MUST have an explicit return type.
64	- Imports MUST be named imports; `import * as` MUST NOT be used.
65	
66	Rationale: explicit, named types keep the contract visible at every boundary and stop
67	untyped data from leaking between layers.
68

70

72	- Every code file MUST stay under 200 lines; split by concern.

  `errorCode` taken from `ErrorCodeEnum`.

Rationale: the gateway, the NATS services, the worker and the frontend stay compatible only
when they all read the same definitions.

### II. Layered Architecture

- Controllers MUST be thin: at most five statements, all delegating to a service. Controllers
  MUST NOT contain logic.
- Every POST, PUT and PATCH handler MUST take a DTO class with class-validator decorators as
  its body.
- Services hold business rules and MUST delegate data access to repositories.
- Database transactions MUST live in repositories only, never in services.
- The gateway MUST NOT hold database access or business rules; it validates input and forwards
  over NATS.
- Every controller, service and provider MUST be registered in exactly one module.
- Source files MUST NOT contain literal ports, hosts, URLs or secrets; configuration comes from
  environment variables read through the config module.
- Every deployable service MUST have a health endpoint: a health message pattern on each NATS
  service, exposed by the gateway as `GET /api/health/<service>`.

Rationale: each layer has one responsibility, so a rule has one place to live and one place
to be tested.

### III. Strict TypeScript

- `interface` MUST NOT be used; use `class` for DTOs and `type` for everything else.
- `any` MUST NOT be used.
- An inline object type MUST NOT be used as a function parameter; define a named DTO class.
- Every repository method MUST have an explicit return type.
- Imports MUST be named imports; `import * as` MUST NOT be used.

Rationale: explicit, named types keep the contract visible at every boundary and stop
untyped data from leaking between layers.

### IV. Small, Self-Describing Files

- File names MUST be kebab-case and describe their purpose.
- Every code file MUST stay under 200 lines; split by concern.
- Comments MUST NOT restate what the code does. A comment is allowed only for a non-obvious
  constraint, in one short line.

Rationale: a file whose name and size reveal its purpose can be found and understood without
opening its neighbours.

### V. Test-First (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

- Every new or modified service MUST have at least one unit test in a `*.spec.ts` file next
  to it.
- The failing test MUST be written before the implementation.

Rationale: a test written first proves the behaviour was missing and that the change added it.

## Safety Constraints

- `.env` and `.env.*` files MUST NOT be read; refer to configuration by variable name.
- Git is local only: no remote, no push, no pull request.
- Dependencies MUST NOT be added.

## Quality Gates

A change is finished only when all three commands pass:

- `pnpm run build`
- `pnpm run lint`
- `pnpm run test`

## Governance

- This constitution supersedes any other practice in this repository. Where another document
  conflicts with it, the constitution wins.
- Amendments are made by editing this file through `/speckit-constitution`, with the change
  recorded in a local commit.
- Versions follow semantic versioning: MAJOR for removing or redefining a principle, MINOR for
  adding a principle or section or materially expanding guidance, PATCH for clarifications and
  wording.
- Every specification, plan, task list and implementation MUST be checked against these
  principles. A violation MUST be fixed, or justified in writing in the plan, before the
  change is considered finished.

     1	# Data Model: No Overlapping Bookings for the Same Room
     2	
     3	**Feature**: `specs/002-prevent-booking-overlap` | **Date**: 2026-11-10
     4	
     5	This change adds a rule, not data. No table, column, constraint, index or migration is added or
     6	changed (FR-022). Everything in `specs/001-room-bookings/data-model.md` still applies; this document
     7	lists only what is new.
     8	
     9	## Booking — table `bookings` (shape unchanged)
    10	
    11	### New rule: no overlap within a room
    12	
    13	Two bookings overlap when all of these hold (FR-001):
    14	
    15	- same `room_id`;
    16	- `starts_at` of each is earlier than `ends_at` of the other;
    17	- they are different rows.
    18	
    19	Spans are half-open, `[starts_at, ends_at)`: a booking that starts when another ends does not
    20	overlap it. Only rows that exist count; `confirmation_status` plays no part (FR-004).
    21	
    22	For a candidate span `[start, end)` in room `R`, a stored booking `b` is in the way when
    23	`b.room_id = R AND b.starts_at < end AND b.ends_at > start`, and, on update, `b.id` is not the
    24	booking being changed. The existing index `IDX_bookings_room_id_starts_at` serves this lookup.
    25	
    26	### Added validation rules
    27	
    28	| Rule | Enforced by | Answer |
    29	|---|---|---|
    30	| A new booking's span is free in its room (FR-005) | claim transaction in `IdempotentBookingRepository`, under the room lock; the service chooses the answer | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` |
    31	| An updated booking's resulting span is free in its room, itself excluded (FR-009, FR-010) | update transaction in `BookingRepository`, under the room lock; the service chooses the answer | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` |
    32	
    33	Both come after every existing rule in the 001 table (FR-008, FR-011).
    34	
    35	### Room lock
    36	
    37	| Property | Value |
    38	|---|---|
    39	| Kind | transaction-scoped advisory lock, waiting (`pg_advisory_xact_lock`) |
    40	| Name | `room:<roomId>`, hashed with `hashtextextended(…, 0)` |
    41	| Taken by | the create claim transaction and the update transaction, before the overlap check |
    42	| Not taken by | list, read, delete, recording a confirmation outcome, a replay |
    43	| Released | at commit or rollback |
    44	
    45	Nothing is stored for the lock.
    46	
    47	## Claim outcomes (create) — one added
    48	
    49	Internal to the `booking` service; not a contract item.
    50	
    51	| Outcome | Condition | Answer |
    52	|---|---|---|
    53	| `CREATED`, `REPLAYED`, `KEY_REUSED`, `IN_PROGRESS` | as in 001 | as in 001 |
    54	| `OVERLAP` *(new)* | the key is free and unclaimed, and the span is taken in the room | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`; no booking, no idempotency row, no job |
    55	
    56	Order inside the claim transaction:
    57	
    58	```text
    59	try-lock key+fingerprint ── not obtained ──▶ IN_PROGRESS
    60	try-lock key ────────────── not obtained ──▶ KEY_REUSED
    61	read stored key ─────────── found ─────────▶ REPLAYED / KEY_REUSED
    62	lock room (waits)
    63	overlap check ───────────── taken ─────────▶ OVERLAP        (nothing written)
    64	insert booking + idempotency row ──────────▶ CREATED
    65	```
    66	
    67	## Update outcomes — new
    68	
    69	Internal to the `booking` service. Class `UpdateBookingResultDto` with `UpdateBookingOutcomeEnum`
    70	and the stored booking (or `null`).
    71	
    72	| Outcome | Condition | Answer |
    73	|---|---|---|
    74	| `NOT_FOUND` | no booking with that id, before or after the wait for the lock | 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING` |
    75	| `INVALID_TIME_RANGE` | resulting `ends_at` not later than resulting `starts_at` | 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` |
    76	| `OVERLAP` | the resulting span is taken by another booking of the room | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`; booking unchanged |
    77	| `UPDATED` | none of the above | 200 with the stored booking |
    78	
    79	The resulting span uses the stored value for a time that was not sent. An update with no fields is
    80	answered by the service before any transaction, as today.
    81	
    82	## Idempotency record — table `idempotency_keys` (unchanged)
    83	
    84	A row is still written only together with a booking. An overlap rejection writes none, so its key
    85	stays usable with any body (FR-007).
    86	
    87	## Room — table `rooms` (read-only, unchanged)
    88	
    89	The scope of the rule. Not read, locked or written by this change; the room lock is a name derived
    90	from the room's id, not a lock on its row.
    91	
    92	## Error code — `ErrorCodeEnum` (the one contract change)
    93	
    94	| Member | Value | Status |
    95	|---|---|---|
    96	| `BOOKING_OVERLAP` | `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` | 409 |
    97	
    98	## Migrations
    99	
   100	None.

     2	
     3	**Feature**: `specs/002-prevent-booking-overlap` | **Date**: 2026-11-10
     4	
     5	This change adds a rule, not data. No table, column, constraint, index or migration is added or
     6	changed (FR-022). Everything in `specs/001-room-bookings/data-model.md` still applies; this document
     7	lists only what is new.
     8	
     9	## Booking — table `bookings` (shape unchanged)
    10	
    11	### New rule: no overlap within a room
    12	
    13	Two bookings overlap when all of these hold (FR-001):
    14	
    15	- same `room_id`;
    16	- `starts_at` of each is earlier than `ends_at` of the other;
    17	- they are different rows.
    18	
    19	Spans are half-open, `[starts_at, ends_at)`: a booking that starts when another ends does not
    20	overlap it. Only rows that exist count; `confirmation_status` plays no part (FR-004).
    21	
    22	For a candidate span `[start, end)` in room `R`, a stored booking `b` is in the way when
    23	`b.room_id = R AND b.starts_at < end AND b.ends_at > start`, and, on update, `b.id` is not the
    24	booking being changed. The existing index `IDX_bookings_room_id_starts_at` serves this lookup.
    25	
    26	### Added validation rules
    27	
    28	| Rule | Enforced by | Answer |
    29	|---|---|---|
    30	| A new booking's span is free in its room (FR-005) | claim transaction in `IdempotentBookingRepository`, under the room lock; the service chooses the answer | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` |
    31	| An updated booking's resulting span is free in its room, itself excluded (FR-009, FR-010) | update transaction in `BookingRepository`, under the room lock; the service chooses the answer | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` |
    32	
    33	Both come after every existing rule in the 001 table (FR-008, FR-011).
    34	
    35	### Room lock
    36	
    37	| Property | Value |
    38	|---|---|
    39	| Kind | transaction-scoped advisory lock, waiting (`pg_advisory_xact_lock`) |
    40	| Name | `room:<roomId>`, hashed with `hashtextextended(…, 0)` |
    41	| Taken by | the create claim transaction and the update transaction, before the overlap check |
    42	| Not taken by | list, read, delete, recording a confirmation outcome, a replay |
    43	| Released | at commit or rollback |
    44	
    45	Nothing is stored for the lock.
    46	
    47	## Claim outcomes (create) — one added
    48	
    49	Internal to the `booking` service; not a contract item.
    50	
    51	| Outcome | Condition | Answer |
    52	|---|---|---|
    53	| `CREATED`, `REPLAYED`, `KEY_REUSED`, `IN_PROGRESS` | as in 001 | as in 001 |
    54	| `OVERLAP` *(new)* | the key is free and unclaimed, and the span is taken in the room | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`; no booking, no idempotency row, no job |
    55	
    56	Order inside the claim transaction:
    57	
    58	```text
    59	try-lock key+fingerprint ── not obtained ──▶ IN_PROGRESS
    60	try-lock key ────────────── not obtained ──▶ KEY_REUSED
    61	read stored key ─────────── found ─────────▶ REPLAYED / KEY_REUSED
    62	lock room (waits)
    63	overlap check ───────────── taken ─────────▶ OVERLAP        (nothing written)
    64	insert booking + idempotency row ──────────▶ CREATED
    65	```
    66	
    67	## Update outcomes — new
    68	
    69	Internal to the `booking` service. Class `UpdateBookingResultDto` with `UpdateBookingOutcomeEnum`
    70	and the stored booking (or `null`).
    71	
    72	| Outcome | Condition | Answer |
    73	|---|---|---|
    74	| `NOT_FOUND` | no booking with that id, before or after the wait for the lock | 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING` |
    75	| `INVALID_TIME_RANGE` | resulting `ends_at` not later than resulting `starts_at` | 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` |
    76	| `OVERLAP` | the resulting span is taken by another booking of the room | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`; booking unchanged |
    77	| `UPDATED` | none of the above | 200 with the stored booking |
    78	
    79	The resulting span uses the stored value for a time that was not sent. An update with no fields is
    80	answered by the service before any transaction, as today.
    81	
    82	## Idempotency record — table `idempotency_keys` (unchanged)
    83	
    84	A row is still written only together with a booking. An overlap rejection writes none, so its key
    85	stays usable with any body (FR-007).
    86	
    87	## Room — table `rooms` (read-only, unchanged)
    88	
    89	The scope of the rule. Not read, locked or written by this change; the room lock is a name derived
    90	from the room's id, not a lock on its row.
    91	
    92	## Error code — `ErrorCodeEnum` (the one contract change)
    93	
    94	| Member | Value | Status |
    95	|---|---|---|
    96	| `BOOKING_OVERLAP` | `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` | 409 |
    97	
    98	## Migrations
    99	
   100	None.

# Research: Rooms List Shows the Right Rooms on Every Page

**Feature**: `specs/003-fix-rooms-pagination` | **Date**: 2026-11-10

This document is the root-cause analysis asked for by FR-007. It was written before any code was
changed: at the time of writing, `git status` shows only this feature's `specs/` folder as new and no
source file as modified.

Method: the request was traced by reading the code from the page to the database call. The stack was
not started for this analysis; the cause is a deterministic calculation, and its result is worked
out below for every reported observation. The live reproduction is scenario 1 of
[quickstart.md](./quickstart.md).

## Root-cause analysis

### Where the defect is

`apps/room/src/room/room.repository.ts`, line 19, in `RoomRepository.findPage`:

```ts
skip: (query.page - 1) * DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE,
take: query.limit,
```

The number of rooms to skip is computed with the constant `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE` (10, from
`@roombook/contract`) instead of the requested page size `query.limit`. The number of rooms to take
uses `query.limit` correctly. The line has been there since the room list was first added (commit
`3a97c50`).

Nothing else on the path changes the page or the page size:

| Step | File | What it does with `page` and `limit` |
|---|---|---|
| Page | `apps/web/src/views/rooms/rooms-page.tsx` | calls `listRooms(pageIndex + 1, rowsPerPage)` and renders `result.items` as received |
| Web client | `apps/web/src/services/room.service.ts` | sends them as query parameters |
| Gateway | `apps/gateway/src/room/room.controller.ts` | validates them as `PageQueryDto` and forwards them over NATS |
| Room controller | `apps/room/src/room/room.controller.ts` | passes them to the service |
| Room service | `apps/room/src/room/room.service.ts` | passes them to the repository |
| Room repository | `apps/room/src/room/room.repository.ts` | **computes `skip` with the wrong factor** |

### Why it happens

The rooms skipped are `(page − 1) × 10` whatever page size was asked for, where FR-001 requires
`(page − 1) × limit`. The two agree only when `page` is 1 (both are 0) or `limit` is 10.

With the 12 seeded rooms in name order:

| Reported observation | Request | Skipped today | Taken | Result today | Explained |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Page 1 is right at every page size | page 1, any limit | (1 − 1) × 10 = 0 | limit | the first `limit` rooms | the factor is multiplied by 0 |
| Page 2 is right at 10 per page | page 2, limit 10 | (2 − 1) × 10 = 10 | 10 | `Room 11`, `Room 12` | the constant equals the limit |
| Page 2 is wrong at 5 per page | page 2, limit 5 | 10, should be 5 | 5 | not `Room 06`–`Room 10` | the constant differs from the limit |
| Page 2 at 5 per page shows exactly `Room 11` and `Room 12` | page 2, limit 5 | 10 | 5 | the 2 rooms left after the first 10 | 12 − 10 = 2 rooms remain |

Consequences at 5 per page: `Room 06` to `Room 10` are never shown, and page 3 skips 20 rooms and is
empty while the page counter still reports 12 rooms.

### Why the existing tests did not catch it

No test asks the code that computes `skip` for a page after the first at a page size other than 10,
which is the only combination where the wrong and the right formula differ.

| Test | What it checks | Why it passes with the defect |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/room/src/room/room.repository.spec.ts` | `findPage({ page: 1, limit: 10 })` → `skip: 0`; `findPage({ page: 2, limit: 10 })` → `skip: 10` | both cases use the default page size, where `(page − 1) × 10` equals `(page − 1) × limit` |
